claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The baseline alloy has high density and insufficient room-temperature ductility.
A minor Si addition followed by tailored heat treatment will precipitate a Si-rich intermetallic phase in the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
The Si-rich secondary phase may be a silicide or Heusler-type phase.
The secondary intermetallic phase will form a continuous or semi-continuous reticulated network along grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
Silicides and related secondary phases in refractory high-entropy alloys can be intrinsically brittle.
Heat treatment below the secondary-phase solvus will preserve network formation while avoiding complete dissolution.
A continuous brittle intermetallic network will force cracks to deflect and branch.
Crack deflection and branching will increase fracture surface area and energy absorption, thereby improving room-temperature ductility.
The Si addition and associated precipitates will increase the bulk density because of the high atomic mass of Si.
Solid-solution hardening primarily raises yield strength through lattice distortion without necessarily changing crack-propagation paths.
The Si-modified alloy will have greater room-temperature compressive fracture strain than the baseline.
The Si-modified alloy will have lower yield strength than the baseline pure solid solution.
The Si-modified alloy will have higher bulk density than the baseline.
The Si modification will shift failure from brittle fracture toward a more ductile mode mediated by crack deflection.
Ductility improvement requires a continuous or semi-continuous secondary-phase network, whereas isolated particles may provide negligible or negative benefit because of stress concentration.
Current thermodynamic databases are insufficiently accurate for predicting L2_1 or Heusler-phase stability in this Hf-containing quinary system.
Hf-containing multicomponent alloys can retain an unresolved Heusler-type phase and form grain-boundary eutectics during homogenization.
The kinetic competition between formation of the desired network and formation of brittle grain-boundary eutectics is unresolved in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr-Si.
A W-added control can provide equivalent solid-solution strengthening without forming a secondary phase.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies only when a continuous or semi-continuous network forms, but the first falsification condition treats reduced ductility in the absence of such a network as falsification. Failure to form the required mediator is an intervention failure or an out-of-boundary case, not a decisive test of the proposed crack-deflection mechanism.
